summary: Hostile audit #12 — LISTENERS: the event input layer

survived.title: dock_events treats any arrival at a trigger value as a NEW dock cycle — a startup, an entity re-add, or an `unavailable` blip mid-cycle re-records the event and increments the durable counter
survived.mechanism: `_handle_dock_event` dedupes only on `new_val == old_val` (line 74), with `old_val = str(old_state.state)... if old_state else ""` (line 72). It never requires that the PREVIOUS value was a real, non-trigger dock state. Three reachable event shapes therefore all read as 'a new cycle started': (a) `old_state is None` — the first state_changed after the dock_status entity is added. The watched entity is NOT ours: adapters/eufy/adapter.py:191 builds `dock_status` from the vacuum entity id, so it belongs to the eufy-clean/robovac_mqtt integration, and manifest.json declares no dependency/after_dependency on it, so eufy_vacuum can register this listener before that entity exists on every HA start. (b) `unknown -> drying` — the brand sensor comes up `unknown` then publishes the in-progress cycle. (c) `unavailable -> drying` / `unavailable -> washing` — an MQTT/cloud blip during a cycle, exactly the transition class HA guarantees will happen. In every case the loop at line 91 matches the trigger set (adapters/eufy/vocabulary.py:78 DOCK_EVENT_TRIGGERS: drying/drying mop/mop drying, washing/washing mop, emptying dust...) and calls `record_dock_event`, which at dock/manager.py:383 unconditionally overwrites `dock_events[vid][event_type] = now` and at :420-424 increments `mop_wash_count`/`dust_empty_count`/`dry_start_count`. The eufy adapter declares `debounce_seconds` for `last_mop_wash` ONLY (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:479-481), so `last_dry_start` and `last_dust_empty` have `debounce = 0.0` -> `should_count = True` with no suppression at all; and even for mop wash the debounce is checked AFTER the timestamp write, so `last_mop_wash` is still reset to the blip time. An X10 Pro Omni dry cycle runs 2-4 hours, so the window for a restart or a blip to land inside one is large and daily. This is the module that diverges: the sibling in listeners/discovery.py:127-131 filters precisely this class ('Only fire on transition INTO docked — filter out ... unknown -> docked startup noise'); dock_events, the only listener of the eight that WRITES durable counters from a raw state arrival, has no such filter.
survived.user_impact: Maintenance data drifts upward silently and permanently: dry-start / dust-empty / mop-wash counts inflate by one per HA restart or connectivity blip that lands inside a dock cycle, and the 'last washed / last dried / last emptied' timestamps shown on the Base Station tab are reset to the moment of the blip rather than the moment of the real cycle. mop_wash_count also feeds the post-job water amendment's `mop_wash_count_at_finalization`, so inflated wash counts propagate into the completed-job water actuals. No error is surfaced anywhere.

survived.title: lifecycle registers a state listener + timer (post-job water amendment) whose unsubs are function-local and unreachable from lifecycle.remove()/async_unload_entry — the only unsub leak among the eight modules
survived.mechanism: Inside the lifecycle handler, `_register_post_job_water_amendment(hass, ...)` (lifecycle.py:390) calls core/water_amendment.py, which at lines 243-246 registers `async_track_state_change_event(hass, [dock_status_entity], _on_dock_change)` plus `async_call_later(hass, timeout_seconds, _on_timeout)` and stores both unsubs in the FUNCTION-LOCAL lists `unsub_listener` / `unsub_timeout` (lines 110-111). Nothing writes them into `hass.data[DOMAIN]`, and `lifecycle.remove()` (lifecycle.py:62-71) pops and cancels only `_job_lifecycle_unsubs` — the single `async_track_state_change_event` from `register()`. So `async_unload_entry`'s `lifecycle.remove(hass)` (__init__.py:480) does not cancel them. The only paths that cancel are `_commit()` firing on the adapter's commit_state or the timeout expiring (default `timeout_seconds=180`, lifecycle.py:388). Every one of the other seven modules stores 100% of what it registers in its hass.data unsub list (discovery even stores the `async_at_started` handle), so this is a single-module asymmetry, not a house style. Reachable window: any mop job finalizes, then within 180 s the config entry is unloaded/reloaded (an options change, a HACS update, `_async_update_listener` firing) or the vacuum is deleted via `_teardown_vacuum`. During that window the orphaned callback keeps consuming dock_status state_changed events against a torn-down entry, and `_on_timeout -> _commit -> hass.async_create_task(_flush_amendment())` performs an executor `os.replace` over the completed-job JSON at `job_path` after the integration has been unloaded. Related: `hass.data[DOMAIN]['_water_amendment_jobs']` (water_amendment.py:71) is never popped by `async_unload_entry`, so the `if not domain_data: hass.data.pop(DOMAIN, None)` at __init__.py:545 can never fire once any mop job has been amended.
survived.user_impact: An unloaded/reloaded integration keeps a live state subscription and a pending timer for up to 180 s and rewrites a completed-job learning file after teardown. Because the leaked `_commit` reads the live water_level entity at fire time, a reload mid-window can stamp `water_amended_at` / `actual_*` water figures derived from post-teardown state onto a finished job record; the user sees no error and no indication the write came from a dead entry.

survived.title: Per-vacuum teardown never re-registers listeners, and the documented 'a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert' invariant is false — discovery keeps running passes for the deleted vacuum and re-creates its setup_progress bucket
survived.mechanism: `_teardown_vacuum` (__init__.py:576-631) deliberately does not touch the listeners, resting on the invariant stated at core/manager.py:1051-1053: 'the global listeners self-correct on the next reload/restart — a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert.' That premise is wrong: the watched entities are built from the vacuum entity id and belong to the BRAND integration (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:190-194), so deleting our device deletes none of them and the subscriptions keep delivering. Four of the eight modules re-derive the vacuum set live from `manager.get_known_vacuum_ids()` on every fire (lifecycle.py:105, pause_timeout.py:68, job_progress.py:64, pose_sampler.py:312) and are genuinely self-correcting; four snapshot it at register() (discovery's `_make_run_pass(vid)` closure at discovery.py:80-96, dock_events' `watched` map at dock_events.py:51-55, job_metrics' `watch_map` at job_metrics.py:77-124, path_blockers' `watch_map` at path_blockers.py:68-91). Three of the four snapshot modules are rescued by accident rather than design — dock_events by `unregister_adapter_config` in `_teardown_vacuum` making `get_adapter_value(...,'dock_events','triggers')` return `{}`; job_metrics because `record_active_job_sensor_value` (jobs/active_job.py:1669) uses `.get()` not `setdefault`. discovery is NOT rescued: its periodic ticker (discovery.py:163-175, adapter-configured interval) and its docked/active-map triggers keep calling `_do()` for the deleted vid, which runs `async_refresh_room_source(hass, vid)` (for Roborock, a `get_maps` service call against a vacuum the user deleted) and `run_discovery_pass` -> `update_drift_history` -> `_get_progress_record` (setup/drift.py:152-159), which unconditionally `setdefault`s `data['setup_progress'][<deleted vid>]` back into storage, then `await manager.async_save()` (discovery.py:88) persists it — silently undoing part of what `remove_vacuum_record` just deleted.
survived.user_impact: After deleting one vacuum from a multi-vacuum install, an orphaned `setup_progress` entry for it is written back to .storage and survives restarts, and a background discovery pass (including a brand service call on Roborock) keeps firing for the removed vacuum until the entry is reloaded or HA restarts. Nothing is user-visible today because the resurrected bucket is empty and `get_known_vacuum_ids()` (manager.py:2966-2969) unions only vacuums/maps/active_jobs — but the invariant the design leans on is not actually held by the code, so any future writer reached from a snapshot-based listener resurrects real data.

survived.title: dock_events.register() never reads the adapter's `dock_events.enabled` flag — a brand that declares enabled:False but inherits triggers still records dock events
survived.mechanism: adapters/config_schema.py:647-654 documents `dock_events.enabled` as 'Whether to record dock events (wash, empty, dry). Set False for brands with no dock actions. Default: False.' The eufy adapter sets it True (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:468). But `dock_events.register()`/`_handle_dock_event` read only `entities.dock_status` (line 53) and `dock_events.triggers` (line 85-91) — `enabled` is never consulted. The only reader anywhere in the component is core/manager.py:3995, where it gates the `supports_base_station` capability flag for the UI. Recording is therefore gated purely on 'a dock_status entity is declared AND a non-empty triggers dict exists'. Both shipped brands happen to be self-consistent (Eufy: enabled + triggers; Roborock: neither block, so `get_adapter_value(..., fallback={})` yields {} and nothing fires), so this is latent today.
survived.user_impact: A future adapter that copies the Eufy dock_events block and flips `enabled: False` to opt out gets the opposite of what it declared: dock events are recorded and counters incremented, while the Base Station UI tab is hidden — so the data accumulates with no surface to inspect or correct it. Fails toward Eufy behaviour, silently, which is the recurring shape of this seam.

survived.title: The exactly-once claim's REFUSAL dict is consumed as a successful finalize — the duplicate EVENT_JOB_FINISHED survived the fix and now carries an all-null payload
survived.mechanism: The shipped exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:702-716) does not raise and does not return None on re-entry — it returns a REFUSAL DICT, {"vacuum_entity_id":..., "finalized": False, "reason": "finalize_in_flight"}. lifecycle.py never inspects `finalized` or `reason`. It logs "Auto-finalized job ... %s", calls mark_active_job_finalized(finalize_result=<refusal>) — which writes finalize_summary with job_id/job_path/used_for_learning/sanity_passed/sanity_flags/status ALL None and finalized_at None — and then fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED because `finalize_result is not None` is true for a refusal. job_finished_event_data (_common.py:225-237) then defaults status to "completed" via outcome.get("status", "completed") while job_id, room_count, duration_minutes, actual_cleaning_minutes, used_for_learning, finalized_at and job_path are all None. Reachability of the second pass is not a lucky interleave: the claim writes only `finalize_claimed_at` into the stored job, it does NOT change active_job["status"], and mark_active_job_finalized (the sole writer of status="completed") runs only AFTER the heavy executor hop in _finalize_claimed. So a second _process task created by any watched-entity change during the finalize window re-reads status=="started", re-reads the same live completion signals, and passes the identical gate. At dock that is the normal case, not an edge: on Eufy the parser sets task_status="Completed" and clears active_cleaning_target in one pass (that pair IS the predicate) and then vacuum->docked and dock_status->drying follow, each now passing the full gate; on Roborock status->charging, binary_sensor cleaning->off and current_room->dock-room land together. HA's eager-start of async_create_task does not rescue this — eager-start only helps when the predicate is not yet satisfied. Ordering makes it worse: the refusal path suspends exactly once (the tracker.end_job executor hop at :339) while the real path is still inside finalize_from_inputs + _auto_record_accuracy, so the BOGUS event normally fires FIRST. This is the exact residual V1 listed as surviving F2 ("EVENT_JOB_FINISHED fires per task"), and it is the same defect shape already open at two SIBLING sites — A5-STR-5 (jobs/active_job.py:2464) and A2-CAN-6 (jobs/active_job.py:2189) — but not at this one, the primary every-run path.
survived.user_impact: The documented public automation trigger `eufy_vacuum_job_finished` (docs/advanced/02-events.md; docs/dev/02-ha-integration.md:438 documents an 11-key contract) fires twice on a normal completed run, and the FIRST of the two claims status "completed" with every data field null. A user automation that notifies "{{ trigger.event.data.room_count }} rooms in {{ trigger.event.data.duration_minutes }} min" renders "None rooms in None min" or throws a template error, then is immediately followed by a second, correct notification. Nothing is logged as an error — the debug line asserts "Auto-finalized job". Additionally mark_active_job_finalized is invoked with the refusal, blanking the stored finalize_summary (all values None); the real finalize normally overwrites it a moment later, but the two paths race on separate executor hops, so on a slow/contended executor the card's post-run summary is left permanently blank — no outcome, no learning verdict, no sanity flags — which is the identical user-visible symptom already recorded for A2-CAN-6.

survived.title: _process tasks are untracked — remove() drops only the subscription, so a config-entry reload orphans an in-flight finalize bound to the dead manager
survived.mechanism: `hass.async_create_task(_process())` creates a task owned by `hass`, not by the config entry, and nothing holds a reference to it. `remove(hass)` (:62-71) pops and calls only the `async_track_state_change_event` unsub — it cannot and does not cancel tasks already spawned. `manager_local` is resolved once from hass.data at :100, at EVENT time, and the `manager_local is None` early return at :101-102 therefore cannot catch a reload that happens later, during the multi-hundred-millisecond await chain (finalize executor hop, accuracy executor hop, tracker.end_job hop, async_save). async_unload_entry (__init__.py:480-487) calls remove() on all eight listeners and tears down the mapping tracker, battery manager, error tracker and adapter coordinator, but cancels no listener tasks. An orphan therefore completes against the torn-down manager: it calls mark_active_job_finalized on the DEAD manager's `data` dict, fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED, and finally `await manager_local.async_save()` — writing the dead manager's snapshot into the Store the freshly-constructed manager also owns. The new manager loaded active_jobs from that Store during setup and still holds the run as status="started", with no `finalize_claimed_at` and no `finalized` flag, so its own lifecycle listener will re-finalize the same run on the next watched change, or the stranded reaper will later book it as `interrupted`. This is the exact mechanism the audit's F1 confirmed for PhaseRunner tasks; the fix landed as a PhaseRunner concern and this sibling spawn site was not covered. phase_runner.py has an ownership check (`_still_ours`); lifecycle.py has no equivalent.
survived.user_impact: Reload the integration (Configure -> options change, HACS update, Dev-Tools reload) in the seconds after a run docks and the run's finalization lands in a manager that is no longer authoritative: the live manager still shows the job as `started`, so the card keeps displaying an in-progress run, manual start stays blocked, and the run is subsequently either finalized a second time or reaped and recorded as `interrupted` rather than `completed` — which changes whether it feeds learning. No error is surfaced on either side.

survived.title: The inline mop-wash detector diverges from the dedicated dock_events listener: hard-coded Eufy wash vocabulary as a fallback, and no same-state guard against attribute-only re-triggers

survived.title: is_job_active() treats a NOT-YET-ADDED / removed job_active entity as "no job running", defeating the Roborock mid-recharge completion guard
survived.mechanism: is_job_active() resolves entities.job_active from the adapter registry, then does `state = hass.states.get(entity_id); if state is None: return False` (lines 138-139) BEFORE the unavailable/unknown handling on line 141. Roborock's entity IDs are pure string derivation (adapters/roborock/entities.py:52 `f"{domain}.{object_id}{suffix}"`, SUFFIX_JOB_ACTIVE="_cleaning"), so `entities.job_active` is ALWAYS declared regardless of whether the HA roborock integration has created binary_sensor.{id}_cleaning yet. The gate this defeats: listeners/lifecycle.py:281-284 is the ONLY suppression of finalization during a mid-job recharge. The shared helper `run_is_in_flight` / `_RUN_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` (jobs/active_job.py:136,160-184) is `("started","paused","external")` and its docstring states the rule explicitly: "Ask run_is_in_flight when the question is about the ROBOT rather than the queue... Observation belongs here — sampling, recording... refusing to observe it is how evidence goes missing." It even names the two copies it knew about (`_SAMPLED_STATUSES`, the inline tuple in `record_pose_sample`); this third one in job_progress was missed. Consequence chain: `manager.maybe_pulse_live_room_refresh` (core/manager.py:4915 → live_refresh/manager.py:112) has exactly ONE caller in the entire package — this ticker (verified by grep). survived.title: `_duration_state_to_seconds` silently treats any unrecognized unit as seconds, and re-resolves the unit per event with no mid-run consistency check
survived.mechanism: The function handles only ms/min/h aliases; every other unit string — including HA's `UnitOfTime.DAYS` ("d"), `WEEKS` ("w"), `MICROSECONDS`, `NANOSECONDS`, and any localized or misspelled unit — falls through to `return int(round(value))`, i.e. is assumed to already be seconds, with no log line. The sibling area path deliberately documents this policy (`cleaning_area_to_m2`, learning/utils.py:44-55: "An unknown or absent unit is assumed to ALREADY be m² ... we never guess a factor"), but for duration the silent default is the unsafe direction: an unhandled larger unit is under-read by its whole factor rather than merely unscaled. Separately, the unit is resolved fresh on every event (job_metrics.py:153-157) and the resulting seconds value is appended to `counter_samples` as an absolute — nothing compares the unit used for sample N against sample N-1. If the entity's `unit_of_measurement` ever changes or appears/disappears mid-run (e.g. a restored state that lacks the attribute until the first live update, with an adapter `cleaning_time_unit` hint present), the buffered series silently mixes two scales, and `counter_segmentation._prepare_window` would read the scale change as a huge increment or a reset. No shipped brand is known to hit this today.

On the two shipped brands the resolved units are "s" (Eufy, absent → seconds) and the adapter hint "min" (Roborock, bare number), both handled correctly and test-covered, so no wrong value reaches a user today. The exposure is that a brand or HA release publishing an unhandled duration unit, or flipping the unit mid-run, produces a silently wrong learned run duration with no warning to diagnose from.

survived.mechanism: `_handle_path_blocker_change` filters only two things: `new_state_obj is None` (entity removal) and `old_state == new_state` (attribute-only tick). survived.title: path_blockers spawns unbounded concurrent `_process` tasks; a second blocker event inside the 30s cancel-confirm window double-cancels and the loser deterministically nulls the run's finalize_summary
survived.mechanism: `hass.async_create_task(_process())` is called for EVERY qualifying state change with no in-flight guard and no task handle kept. `async_cancel_active_job` does not mark the job before it awaits: it checks `status in {started, paused}` (jobs/active_job.py:2189), then awaits `return_to_base` and polls for a terminal state for up to `_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S = 30` seconds (line 2218) before `mark_active_job_finalized` runs. Throughout that whole window the stored status is unchanged, so a second `_process` — a different blocker entity changing, or the SAME sensor bouncing (the clearing pass pops `last_path_block_signature` at run_plan.py:1675, so the re-trigger is not deduped) — passes the same guard and starts a SECOND cancel: a second `vacuum.return_to_base` and a second 30s poll. Both then call `finalize_learning_for_active_job`. The exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:690-719) protects the learning record: the second call returns `{"finalized": False, "reason": "already_finalized"|"finalize_in_flight"}` with NO `completed_job` key. But `async_cancel_active_job` still runs `mark_active_job_finalized` unconditionally (line 2272) with that refusal dict, and jobs/active_job.py:2042-2076 then writes `finalized_at = None` and a `finalize_summary` whose `job_id`, `job_path`, `status`, `used_for_learning`, `sanity_passed`, `sanity_flags` are all None. The refused task is by construction the one that reached finalize LAST, so the null summary is always the last write. It also returns `cancelled: True`, so path_blockers.py:159 fires a second EVENT_JOB_FINISHED built by `_common.job_finished_event_data`, which defaults `status` to `"completed"` when `completed_job` is absent.

survived.title: The 1-minute reap ticker has no in-flight guard while each reap blocks up to ~35s, so two reapable slots guarantee overlapping ticks and a duplicate cancel
survived.mechanism: `_handle_pause_timeout_tick` fires every 60s and unconditionally does `hass.async_create_task(_process())` — no flag, no handle, no check that the previous tick's task finished. `_process` walks every (vacuum, map) SEQUENTIALLY and each paused-timeout reap awaits `async_cancel_active_job`, which is a blocking `return_to_base` service call plus a poll loop bounded by `_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S = 30` (jobs/active_job.py:2218-2237). With two reapable slots (two managed vacuums whose paused jobs time out on the same tick — the normal outcome after a power event or an HA outage), one pass takes ~70s and the next tick fires while it is still inside the second slot's poll. `get_paused_job_timeout_report` (jobs/active_job.py:2286-2329) re-reads the stored job, which still says `status: paused` with the original `paused_at` (nothing is written until the cancel completes), so it returns a report again and a SECOND `async_cancel_active_job` starts for the same slot. clean_areas: Double-registration: all eight modules (discovery, dock_events, job_metrics, job_progress, lifecycle, path_blockers, pause_timeout, pose_sampler) call remove(hass) as the first statement of register(hass). Verified line by line; calling register() twice cannot leak or double-fire.

Unsub key hygiene: each module uses a unique hass.data[DOMAIN] key, remove() pops it (so the key can never go stale), each remove() wraps unsub() in try/except, and async_unload_entry (__init__.py:480-487) calls remove() for all eight in the same order they were registered.

Module-global unsub storage is CORRECT for this integration, not a multi-entry bug: config_flow.py sets unique_id=DOMAIN and calls _abort_if_unique_id_configured, so exactly one config entry can exist; multi-vacuum support lives inside that single entry (one manager, one adapter coordinator). The single-instance guard is load-bearing for every hass.data[DOMAIN][...] slot in listeners/.

path_blockers re-entrancy: _handle_room_update calls register(hass) -> remove(hass) -> manager.unregister_room_update_callback() from INSIDE manager._notify_rooms_updated. Safe on both counts — _notify_rooms_updated iterates `list(self._room_update_callbacks)` (a copy, core/manager.py:629) so mutation during iteration cannot raise or skip, and _normalized_managed_rooms_with_automation (rooms/access_graph.py:196-229) is read-only and fires no notify, so there is no recursion. The room callback is stored in hass.data and unregistered by remove().

discovery closure binding: the per-vacuum callbacks (_on_vacuum_state, _on_active_map, _on_tick) all bind run_pass via a default argument, and run_pass itself is produced by the _make_run_pass(vid) factory — the classic late-binding-loop-variable bug is genuinely absent, and the comment claiming it is handled matches the code. async_at_started's return value is appended to the unsub list rather than dropped.

discovery._on_vacuum_state's transition filter (`new_state == 'docked' and old_state != 'docked'`) correctly suppresses attribute-only re-fires and the unknown->docked startup edge — this is the behaviour dock_events lacks (REG-1).

Live re-derivation of the vacuum set in lifecycle, pause_timeout, job_progress and pose_sampler: each iterates manager.get_known_vacuum_ids() on every fire rather than a register-time snapshot, so all four self-correct after a vacuum is removed and are inert for a deleted one.

lifecycle._handle_lifecycle_change re-reads DATA_RUNTIME from hass.data on every event and returns when it is None, so a leaked callback firing against a torn-down entry is a no-op. dock_events, job_metrics, path_blockers and pause_timeout do the same re-read.

job_metrics is safe against post-delete storage resurrection: record_active_job_sensor_value (jobs/active_job.py:1669) and record_counter_sample (:1702) both use .get() on the active_jobs bucket, never setdefault, and return False when it is absent.

The register() domain-data divergence (job_progress.py:57 and pose_sampler.py:291 use hass.data.setdefault(DOMAIN, {}); the other six use hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {})) is inert, not a leak: in the only case where .get would hand back a throwaway dict, DATA_RUNTIME is absent from it too, so register() returns at the manager-is-None check before ever writing the unsub list. Worth normalising, but there is no reachable defect today.

pose_sampler's cadence resolution (_room_attribution_interval_s) is read at register() time, which is AFTER register_brand_adapter runs for every vacuum in async_setup_entry (__init__.py:307 vs :404), so the adapter registry is always populated before any listener reads it. An absent entity, a None state, and 'unknown'/'unavailable' all yield None rather than a bogus 0.0, so the engine's swept_area_min_m2 gate cannot mis-fire on a raw ft² value.

_SAMPLED_STATUSES vs the rest of the integration's in-flight predicates — I traced the KNOWN LEAD to its end and the divergence is EXACTLY the deferred one, nothing more. _DISPATCHED_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES = ('started','paused') and _RUN_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES = that + ('external',) (jobs/active_job.py:130-136). The await gap in _sample_vacuum_once is properly closed. The status check at line 252 is followed by an await (the live-pose read) before record_pose_sample at 264, so the run CAN be finalized in between — but record_pose_sample re-validates status in ('external','started') AND started_at/not ended_at (jobs/active_job.py:1775-1778) before appending, and mark_active_job_finalized sets status='completed'. A run finalized during the pose await therefore cannot receive a post-finalize sample. This is the correct pattern (re-check at the write, not at the read).

register()/remove() unsub lifecycle — no leak and no double-fire. register() calls remove(hass) as its first statement (line 289), remove() pops the stored unsub list from hass.data and cancels each inside a try/except, and the integration is provably SINGLE-ENTRY (config_flow.py:44-51 sets unique_id=DOMAIN then _abort_if_unique_id_configured), so the module-global hass.data key can never hold two entries' timers. The reload path (async_unload_entry -> pose_sampler.remove, then async_setup_entry -> pose_sampler.register at __init__.py:404/486) is symmetric, and _handle_pose_tick re-reads manager.get_known_vacuum_ids() live rather than capturing a snapshot, so a vacuum added after registration is picked up on the next tick.

_room_attribution_source / _can_sample source dispatch — correct per-source gating. The 'live_pose' default for a block predating the key is genuinely back-compatible, the live_pose branch requires map_state_source.live_pose to be a dict, and a vacuum whose declared source's signal is absent is refused rather than silently buffering an all-None current_room. get_adapter_config returning None is handled with `or {}` at every call site (lines 70, 89, 101, 244).

_resolve_managed_room_id sentinel + slug handling faithfully mirrors its stated sibling ActiveJobTracker._resolve_native_target_room_id (jobs/active_job.py:1120-1166): identical sentinel set {unknown, unavailable, none, null}, identical slug derivation (explicit `slug` else slugify_room_name of name|room_name), identical 'unmatched name -> None' transit semantics. The deliberate difference — matching ALL managed rooms rather than the job's queue targets — is correct for an external run, which has no targets. slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:11-36) is NFC-normalized and script-agnostic, so it does not collapse non-Latin names to a shared empty slug.

End-of-run return-to-dock ticks are handled correctly end to end. _is_parked deliberately does NOT null 'returning'/'navigating' (Eufy) or 'returning_home'/'docking' (Roborock, vocabulary.py:16-26), so those ticks record a room — but _swept_area_by_room sums only POSITIVE per-tick cleaning_area deltas (room_attribution_engines.py:177-198), which stay ~0 during the return, and _classify's robust branch gates 'cleaned' on swept >= swept_area_min_m2 (line 227-231). I verified the claim in the _is_parked docstring rather than trusting it: a transit-only room is correctly labelled transit, not cleaned.

async_get_map_live_pose's return contract is honoured. pose.get('present') at line 201 sits OUTSIDE the try/except, which would be an unguarded AttributeError if the coordinator could return None — I read every return path in mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:500-528 and all five are dict literals. The 'not present -> return None (skip the tick)' choice is also right: skipping beats writing a fabricated sample when no live map decoded.

job_metrics._handle_metrics_change guard chain (job_metrics.py:132-148) — correct and complete. It filters unwatched entity_ids, returns on new_state=None (entity removal), returns on the unavailable/unknown/None sentinels, and — notably — RE-READS the manager from hass.data on every event rather than closing over the register-time instance, so a manager swap mid-session cannot leave it writing into a dead object. Every numeric conversion is inside a try/except (TypeError, ValueError). Cross-checked against the eight documented negative-path cases in tests/integration/test_listeners_job_metrics_negative.py (JMN-1..JMN-8).

Attribute-only and duplicate state_changed events are genuinely harmless here — I chased this as the primary hypothesis and it does not hold. `async_track_state_change_event` does fire on attribute-only ticks and on an `unavailable -> same numeric value` recovery, and `_handle_metrics_change` has no old/new comparison, so it re-records the value and appends a duplicate counter sample. But counter_segmentation._prepare_window (lines 179-190) builds `incs` only where `ct > last_ct` (STRICTLY rising), so a repeated value creates no increment and therefore cannot break a wash_plateau/transit gap — the gap is measured between increments, not between samples. `area_at`/`batt_at` (lines 167-177) are bisect lookups over monotone series, so a duplicate at a later timestamp returns the same value. The 2000-sample cap (jobs/active_job.py:108) is far above a real run's ~500 samples, so duplicate churn cannot rotate the run's early data out. No finding.

Counter RESET handling is correct end-to-end for the run-start case, and a backwards step cannot become a negative or huge delta. The listener records `0` verbatim (it is not one of the filtered sentinels), which is exactly what _prepare_window needs: counter_segmentation.py:151-158 trims the window to the LAST `ct == 0` sample, dropping a stale pre-reset sample carried over from the previous job instead of computing a giant delta across the reset. A drop that does not reach 0 also cannot produce a negative increment, because `incs` only appends on `ct > last_ct` (line 188) and simply re-baselines `last_ct`. The related live-observed Eufy cleaning_area re-baseline (learning/room_attribution_engines.py:184-187, "fell 21.5->10.8") is independently handled by clamping each tick's delta at 0.

job_progress cannot exceed 100% or divide by zero. core/manager.py:3311-3318: `estimated_minutes = max(float(room.get("minutes", 0.0) or 0.0), 1.0)` floors the divisor before any division; `elapsed_minutes = min(current_room_elapsed_minutes, estimated_minutes)` caps the numerator; `progress_percent = max(min(int((elapsed_minutes / estimated_minutes) * 100), 99), 0)` clamps both ends. A completed room is set to a literal 100 without arithmetic. `remaining_minutes` uses `max(..., 0.0)`. Verified there is no other percent computation in the snapshot path.

job_progress register/remove lifecycle is leak-free and reload-safe. `register` calls `remove` first (line 55), stores its unsub list under a module-owned key in hass.data[DOMAIN] (line 119), and `async_unload_entry` calls `job_progress.remove(hass)` (__init__.py:485) — so a config-entry reload tears the interval timer down before re-arming it, with no double-fire and no orphaned unsub. Per-map isolation is also correct: the `map_id_str == "unknown"` skip (line 67) and the try/except around `get_job_progress_snapshot` (lines 93-104) mean one bad map logs and `continue`s rather than killing the tick for every other vacuum/map. The same register/remove symmetry holds for job_metrics (lines 47-56, 68).

cleaning_time unit precedence is correct as written and fully test-covered for both shipped brands: the entity's own `unit_of_measurement` wins, the adapter's `cleaning_time_unit` is a fallback that applies only to a bare-number sensor, and absence means seconds. Confirmed against adapters/roborock/adapter.py:214 (`"cleaning_time_unit": "min"`), the Eufy adapter (declares none -> seconds), and the four cases at tests/integration/test_listeners_job_metrics_negative.py:312-364 including the entity-unit-wins control. The comment block at job_metrics.py:88-95 accurately describes what the code does — I verified it rather than trusting it.

cleaning_area normalization is correct and shared. job_metrics.py:158-164 routes through `learning.utils.cleaning_area_to_m2` with the live entity unit, so an imperial HA presenting Eufy's cleaning_area in ft2 is converted to canonical m2 while Roborock's m2 passes through unscaled, and a None return (blank/unparseable) early-returns WITHOUT recording a misleading zero. This is the same helper the finalizer's fallback path uses (learning/job_finalizer.py:545), so the live-push and fallback-read paths cannot disagree on units.

The `unknown`/`unavailable` state is correctly distinguishable from zero at this layer: the sentinel check at job_metrics.py:141 returns before any write, so the last good value is preserved rather than being clobbered with a 0, while a genuine "0" state is recorded as 0. The finalizer's `_safe_int(..., None)` / `_safe_float(..., None)` reads (learning/job_finalizer.py:551-560) then correctly treat an absent key as "listener never fired" and fall through to the live sensor read.

path_blockers.py:39-61 register/remove idempotency — register() calls remove() first, remove() pops both the unsub list and the room-update callback from hass.data[DOMAIN], and the whole re-registration is SYNCHRONOUS, so no state_changed event can slip through the gap between tearing down the old subscription and installing the new one.

path_blockers.py:93-99 self-re-registration on room config change — `_handle_room_update` calls register(hass) re-entrantly from inside manager._notify_rooms_updated, which iterates `list(self._room_update_callbacks)` (core/manager.py:629), a copy. Unregistering the running callback and appending its replacement mid-notify is therefore safe: no skipped callback, no double-fire, no mutation-during-iteration.

path_blockers.py:116 attribute-only filter — `old_state == new_state` correctly suppresses the attribute-only state_changed events that async_track_state_change_event delivers, so a blocker entity whose attributes tick (e.g. battery level on a contact sensor) does not re-run the report.

path_blockers.py:119 and pause_timeout.py:62 — both re-fetch the manager from hass.data inside the callback instead of closing over the one captured at register time, so a config-entry reload cannot leave a listener acting through a dead manager. (discovery.py does NOT do this — see GUARD-6.)

path_blockers.py:123-194 — `active_job` and the report are both read synchronously before the first await, and `get_runtime_path_block_report` returns None unless status is started/paused (run_plan.py:1529), so there is no None-deref on `active_job.get(...)` and no torn read between the two lookups. The pause branch's `already_paused` short-circuit (line 144) is correct.

pause_timeout.py — the two reaps are mutually exclusive by construction: the paused reap requires status `paused` and the stranded reap requires status `started`, and `_clear_stranded_stamp` (jobs/active_job.py:2331-2337) drops the stamp on any other status so a transient dock never accrues grace toward a false reap.

dock_events.py:51-59 brand isolation — Roborock's adapter omits the `dock_events` block, so `get_adapter_value(..., "dock_events", "triggers", fallback={})` returns {} and the trigger loop is inert; no Eufy dock vocabulary leaks into the Roborock path.
dock_events.py:98-106 — the dry_duration read guards `unknown`/`unavailable`/`""` before recording, so a stale duration select cannot poison last_dry_duration with a sentinel string.

discovery.py:80-96 and 118-169 closure binding — `_make_run_pass(vid)` plus the `_run_pass=run_pass` default-argument capture in `_on_vacuum_state`/`_on_active_map`/`_on_tick`, and the `_run=run_pass` capture in the async_at_started lambda, all correctly bind per-vacuum. There is no late-binding loop-variable bug anywhere in this module, including the deferred at-started callback where it would have been easiest to get wrong.

discovery.py:106-114 — the config_entry_reload pass is deferred to async_at_started and wrapped in @callback so it lands on the event loop rather than the executor; the reasoning in the comment matches the code.

discovery.py — the auto-discovery path is READ-ONLY with respect to room records. `run_discovery_pass` (setup/drift.py:515-556) reads the room list and touches only `setup_progress[...].room_drift_history` counters; `discover_rooms_for_vacuum` (rooms/room_discovery.py:136-206) performs no writes. Audit #10's auto-enable / auto-approve room writes are NOT reachable from any auto-discovery trigger, so a rediscovery firing mid-run cannot mutate rooms under a running job.

rooms/source_refresh.py:248-254 — `async_refresh_room_source` skips the get_maps service call when the target vacuum reads unavailable/unknown, so the `vacuum_docked` trigger firing during a reconnect degrades to the cached source instead of logging a spurious 'did not match any entities' failure.
verifier_notes:
All 30 findings survived verification; I could not kill any outright, which is itself a signal about this batch's quality — the finders cited line numbers that resolved and guards that I re-read rather than took on faith. What I did instead was correct five severities and kill four SUB-claims inside otherwise-real findings, plus flag two duplicate pairs.

SEVERITY CORRECTIONS (5):
- A1-REG-1 HIGH->MEDIUM. Its propagation claim is wrong: `actual_mop_wash_count` comes from `observed_mop_wash_count` via learning/job_finalizer.py:204, NOT from dock/manager.py's `mop_wash_count`. Strip that and the harm is maintenance counters + Base Station timestamps.
- A3-COMMON-2 MEDIUM->LOW. Purely latent (no shipped adapter reaches it), same class as the LOW-rated A3-COMMON-3 / A1-REG-4.
- A4-POSE-2 MEDIUM->LOW. The HA mechanism is real (I read event.py:1637-1643 — `_schedule_timer()` precedes a background, un-awaited dispatch), but the Roborock native path is fully synchronous so it cannot overlap at all, and no measurement shows a live_pose tick exceeding 2.0 s.
- A4-POSE-3 MEDIUM->LOW. The dead-fallback is structurally real, but the proposed Roborock trigger is weak: task_status and current_room are served by the SAME roborock coordinator, so when one reads unavailable the other does too and `_resolve_managed_room_id` returns None — no dock-room pollution. The real exposure is future-brand / entity-add ordering.
- A5-METRICS-1 HIGH->MEDIUM. The gate omission and the single-caller fact are confirmed, but "durably skewed per-room learning" is unproven; dwell_min_ticks 3 x 5.0 s bounds the boundary error against a 15-30 s native cadence. Confirmed harms: no Lever B pulse and no progress-tick event on external runs.

SUB-CLAIMS KILLED inside real findings:
